newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK C.BANK SETS 1-DAY REPO TENDER.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK C.BANK SETS 1-DAY REPO TENDER.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Monday it had set a tender for a one-day securities repurchase for 10 a.m. (0900 GMT), offering banks liquidity at a fixed volume of 1.5 billion crowns.
The NBS said in a statement that the American-style tender would have a minimum rate of 9.7 percent.
At the NBS's last overnight repurchase tender, its first, the average rate was 10.53 percent.
According to official NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector is short of liquidity, with banks' minimum reserve demands fulfilled at 97.89 percent as of Sunday.
The NBS holds tenders on a daily basis, if needed, at 10 a.m. (0900 GMT), instead of quoting securities repo and reverse repo rates.
Tender results are released by 11 a.m. (1000 GMT) with allocations following later in the day.
